name: Joseph Stalin
kicker: Soviet dictator who industrialized by terror · Led the USSR to victory in WWII
briefing: Joseph Stalin was born in a small Georgian town and climbed from bank-robbing revolutionary to the iron-fisted dictator of the Soviet Union for nearly thirty years. His Five-Year Plans rushed the USSR into the industrial age, but forced collectivization and the Great Purge killed millions of his own people. He then led the Soviets through World War II, helping defeat Hitler and making the USSR a postwar superpower.
answerHtml: Joseph Stalin (or Iosif Stalin; prompt on Dzhugashvili or Jughashvili alone)

tossups.p: This leader’s agricultural adviser Trofim Lysenko [“lih-SENG-koh”] rejected Mendelian genetics and made overblown claims about “vernalization.” As a young revolutionary, this man studied for the priesthood at a seminary in Tiflis [“tih-FLEES”] before helping rob banks to fund the Bolsheviks. He later had the city of Tsaritsyn renamed in his own honor.
tossups.r: After Vladimir Lenin’s death in 1924, this man outmaneuvered rivals such as Leon Trotsky for control of the Soviet Union. For 10 points, name this Communist dictator who led the USSR through World War II.

tossups.p: This leader’s secret police executed thousands of captured Polish military officers in the Katyn [“KAH-tin”] Forest massacre of 1940. He also refused to trade his own son, captured by the Germans in 1941, for enemy prisoners of war. Late in his rule, he ordered the execution of Jewish writers and artists in the so-called Night of the Murdered Poets.
tossups.r: His regime’s forced collectivization of farms caused a famine, the Holodomor [“hoh-loh-doh-MOR”], that killed millions in Ukraine. For 10 points, name this dictator who ruled the Soviet Union during World War II.

tossups.p: This man’s secret police chief Nikolai Yezhov [“YEH-zhof”] was later edited out of official photographs after being purged himself. Following the 1934 assassination of Communist official Sergey Kirov, this leader launched show trials that grew into the Great Purge. He took a revolutionary alias that means “man of steel” in Russian.
tossups.r: His government signed a 1939 nonaggression pact with Adolf Hitler that divided up Poland, only to be invaded by Germany in 1941’s Operation Barbarossa. For 10 points, name this Soviet leader who succeeded Vladimir Lenin.

tossups.p: This ruler’s Order No. 227 threatened to punish Red Army soldiers who retreated without permission during World War II. His Five-Year Plans, beginning in 1928, rushed the Soviet Union through industrialization and ended Lenin’s New Economic Policy. He accused mostly Jewish doctors of plotting to kill him in the so-called Doctors’ Plot.
tossups.r: He sent huge numbers of political prisoners to the Gulag, his system of forced-labor camps. For 10 points, name this Communist dictator who led the USSR to victory in World War II.

tossups.p: This leader had his exiled rival Leon Trotsky assassinated in Mexico City in 1940. He had the Russian city of Tsaritsyn renamed after himself in 1925.

trap.title: Stalin, or Stalingrad, or Lenin?
trap.body: Stalin and the Battle of Stalingrad share clues like the Sixth Army, Operation Uranus, and the Eastern Front, since the city was named after him. Stalin is also easy to mix up with his predecessor Vladimir Lenin (who died in 1924, before the Five-Year Plans and the purges) and with his murdered rival Leon Trotsky.
trap.fix: “Name this leader” or “this dictator” wants Stalin; “name this battle” wants Stalingrad. Lenin never ruled during World War II, and Trotsky was Stalin’s victim, not the dictator himself. “Dzhugashvili,” his birth name alone, earns a prompt.
trap.line: Real answer line: Joseph Stalin (accept Iosif Stalin, Ioseb/Iosif Dzhugashvili, or Joseph Jughashvili)
